newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Rebels seize last Albanian stronghold in south.
newsitem.headline: Rebels seize last Albanian stronghold in south.

text.p: Albanian rebels seized this town on Saturday, the last government stronghold in the south, putting newly-arrived troops to flight and seizing thousands of weapons, eyewitnesses and diplomats told Reuters.
In a humiliating defeat for President Sali Berisha, about six helicopters of reinforcement took to flight almost as soon as they landed and their one-star general was arrested, the eyewitnesses said.
The fresh troops, at least a company of 120 men, ran off to surrounding forests and hills after being confronted by rebels and angry residents at the town square, they said.
"Gjirokaster is now under the control of the rebels," an official who requested anonymity said.

About 30 km (20 miles) from the Greek border, Gjirokaster was the last government stronghold in southern Albania and its fall means any effort by the army to stamp out the revolt which has swept the region will be much more difficult.
Most of the government troops had retreated in disarray and were trapped in the Ayia Triada monastery, two km (one mile) east of the town.

The rebels, who already control about two dozen captured tanks, seized four more during the Gjirokaster showdown and were driving them towards the monastery, a Reuters correspondent at the scene said.
The rebels had also stormed and ransacked the army base just north of Gjirokaster, seizing some 10,000 weapons while officers and soldiers stood by watching, a Reuters Television crew said.

There were no immediate reports of injuries and the capture of Gjirokaster appeared to be bloodless. Rebels raced through the town in cars, firing wildly in the air and celebrating their victory, eyewitnesses said.
